cohort: 260 women in the postpartum period at Bertha Gxowa district hospital, South Africa
finding: Women in the postpartum period reported varying levels of satisfaction with different aspects of care, with high satisfaction in privacy and cleanliness but low satisfaction with pain relief during labor (especially vaginal delivery) and involvement in decision-making.
mod_finding: Participants who had a cesarean section were significantly more likely to report being satisfied with pain relief during labor compared to those who had a vaginal delivery.
